pk.context: 40 mg subcutaneous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colorless solution in a single-dose prefilled pen

tell: Peak serum level comes about 5.5 days after a subcutaneous dose, and the label does not approve intravenous use.

clues.text: About 64% of a subcutaneous dose reaches the circulation. Systemic clearance is about 12 mL/hr, with a trend toward higher clearance in the presence of anti-drug antibodies.
A sterile, preservative-free solution of a protein of 1330 amino acids, with a molecular weight of about 148 kilodaltons.
Approved under a BLA as single-dose pens and syringes of 10 to 80 mg, dosed every other week or every week.

Boxed for serious infections, including reactivation of latent tuberculosis, and for malignancy. Injection site reactions are the most common reaction; clinical flare is the commonest cause of discontinuation.
Rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and Crohn's disease, among others.
Binds TNF-alpha specifically and blocks its interaction with the p55 and p75 TNF receptors. It does not bind lymphotoxin.
The generic name begins with A and has ten letters.
